steps.title: Define the core microservices patterns we'll implement
steps.instruction: Create a function named listMicroservicesPatterns that returns an array of strings containing these five patterns: API Gateway, Service Discovery, Circuit Breaker, Event-Driven Communication, and Database per Service.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns an array with the five pattern names as strings.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function is defined that returns an array containing the five specified microservices patterns.
successCriteria: The function listMicroservicesPatterns exists and returns an array with exactly these five strings: 'API Gateway', 'Service Discovery', 'Circuit Breaker', 'Event-Driven Communication', 'Database per Service'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the core microservices patterns we'll explore in this lesson.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function returns an array with all five pattern names exactly as specified.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a function named listMicroservicesPatterns that returns an array containing the five specified patterns.

steps.title: Set up the API Gateway pattern structure
steps.instruction: Create a function named APIGateway that will act as the single entry point for routing requests to microservices.
steps.hint: Define a function with the name APIGateway that returns a placeholder value for now.
steps.seedCode:
// Create your function here

// Create the APIGateway function below
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a function named APIGateway defined, ready to implement routing logic in later steps.
successCriteria: A function named APIGateway is created and returns a value (like null).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the API Gateway structure. This function will serve as the single entry point for client requests to various microservices.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a function named exactly 'APIGateway' and it returns something (even null).
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating a function named APIGateway. Please define a function with that name that returns a value.

steps.title: Initialize service registry for Service Discovery
steps.instruction: Create a service registry object that will track available microservices and their endpoints. Name it 'serviceRegistry' and initialize it as an empty object.
steps.hint: Define a constant variable named 'serviceRegistry' and set it to an empty object {} to start tracking services.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: creating a registry object
const userRegistry = {};
steps.expectedOutcome: A service registry object is created and ready to store microservice information.
successCriteria: The 'serviceRegistry' object is defined as an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the service registry object. This will serve as the foundation for service discovery.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created an object named 'serviceRegistry' and initialized it as empty.
steps.feedbackWrong: The service registry object wasn't created correctly. Create a constant named 'serviceRegistry' and set it to an empty object {}.

steps.title: Define Circuit Breaker pattern logic
steps.instruction: Create a function named CircuitBreaker that monitors service health and fails fast when services are down. The function should take a service name and return a status.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts a service name parameter and returns a status string like 'open', 'closed', or 'half-open'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CircuitBreaker function is defined that can be used to check service health and prevent cascading failures.
successCriteria: The CircuitBreaker function is defined with a service name parameter and returns a status.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the Circuit Breaker pattern logic. This function will help prevent cascading failures by monitoring service health.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your CircuitBreaker function accepts a service name parameter and returns a status value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CircuitBreaker function isn't properly defined. It should be a function that takes a service name and returns a status to monitor service health.

steps.title: Set up Event-Driven Communication infrastructure
steps.instruction: Create a function named EventBus that will serve as a simple event bus for services to publish and subscribe to events.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns an object with methods like publish and subscribe to handle events.
steps.expectedOutcome: The EventBus function is defined and ready to be implemented with publish and subscribe methods.
successCriteria: The EventBus function is created and returns an object with publish and subscribe methods.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the EventBus function. This will allow services to communicate asynchronously through events.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the EventBus function, but make sure it returns an object with publish and subscribe methods.
steps.feedbackWrong: The EventBus function is not correctly defined. Ensure it returns an object with publish and subscribe methods.

steps.title: Implement Database per Service pattern
steps.instruction: Create a function named DatabasePerService that demonstrates separate database connections for different services.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns an object with isolated database connections for each service.
steps.expectedOutcome: A DatabasePerService function is created that returns separate database connections for different services.
successCriteria: The DatabasePerService function is defined and returns an object with at least two different service database connections.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the Database per Service pattern by creating separate database connections for different services.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it returns an object with distinct database connections for at least two different services.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DatabasePerService function is not properly implemented. Create a function that returns separate database connections for different services.

steps.title: Create sample microservices to demonstrate patterns
steps.instruction: Create a UserService function that returns a simple string describing its purpose.
steps.hint: Define a function named UserService that returns a string like 'UserService: manages user data'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a UserService function that returns a descriptive string, demonstrating a basic microservice.
successCriteria: A UserService function is defined and returns a string describing its purpose.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the UserService microservice. This demonstrates how individual services are defined in a microservices architecture.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the UserService, but make sure it returns a descriptive string about its purpose.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UserService function is not properly defined or doesn't return a string. Try creating a function named UserService that returns a description.

steps.title: Wire API Gateway to route requests to services
steps.instruction: Inside the APIGateway function, add logic to route incoming requests to the appropriate microservice based on the request path. Use the service registry to find services.
steps.hint: Check the request path and call the corresponding service function (like UserService) if the path matches.
steps.expectedOutcome: The APIGateway function now contains routing logic that uses the service registry to direct requests to the correct microservice.
successCriteria: APIGateway checks the request path and calls the appropriate service function (e.g., UserService for '/users').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wired the API Gateway to route requests based on the path, demonstrating the API Gateway pattern in action.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some routing logic, but make sure to check the request path and call the correct service function from the registry.
steps.feedbackWrong: The routing logic is missing or incorrect. The APIGateway should examine the request path and route to the appropriate microservice.

steps.title: Register services with Service Discovery
steps.instruction: Add a registerService method to the serviceRegistry object that stores services by name.
steps.hint: You can add a method to the serviceRegistry object that takes a service name and service function as parameters and stores them.
steps.expectedOutcome: The serviceRegistry object now has a registerService method that can store services for discovery.
successCriteria: serviceRegistry has a registerService method that accepts name and service parameters and stores them.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added service registration capability to the service registry.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the registerService method properly stores the service in the registry object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The serviceRegistry object should have a registerService method that stores services by name.

steps.title: Test the complete microservices patterns implementation
steps.instruction: Simulate a request through the API Gateway to test the complete microservices patterns implementation.
steps.hint: Call the APIGateway function with a sample request object that includes a path property to route to a service.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test function that calls APIGateway with a sample request to verify the routing works.
successCriteria: The test function calls APIGateway with a request object containing a path property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully simulated a request through the API Gateway to test the microservices patterns.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your test function calls APIGateway with a request object that has a path property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test function should call APIGateway with a request object to simulate routing.
